content: The test image shows young soybean seedlings that are severely wilted and dead — brown, papery, curled leaves on dark stems, at early seedling stage. This suggests a damping-off or root rot disease. Top candidates: Pythium_damping_off, Phytophthora, Rhizoctonia.

The test image shows dead seedlings with brown, dried leaves still attached to dark stems in field soil — exactly matching Phytophthora's diagnostic: "leaves typically stay attached after plant death" and brown-to-dead wilted plants. The Phytophthora reference collage (top-left and bottom-left panels) is a near-perfect visual match.

Pythium shows very early-stage rotted cotyledons/seeds, and Rhizoctonia shows stem lesions — neither matches as well.
